title: Coroner's jury supports treatment centre
article: At times tearful testimony about the tragic death of 48-year-old Debra Marie Coon on Mar. 14, 2008, led a coroner's jury to seven recommendations.

But before making those recommendations, the five person jury found Ms. Coon died accidentally on Mar. 14, 2008 in Victoria General Hospital, after being at Port Hardy Hospital and in cells at the Port Hardy RCMP detachment.
The immediate cause of death was acute subdural hematoma caused by bumping her head, said the jury.
Four recommendations were aimed at the Vancouver Island Health Authority (VIHA) which operates Port Hardy Hospital.

VIHA should refit the observation room in Port Hardy Hospital "to ensure safe observation of patients who are mentally ill or intoxicated" and then "provide trained staff" to operate it, said the jury in two of its recommendations.

One other piece of equipment needed at Port Hardy Hospital is "blood-alcohol testing equipment to better assist in the assessment of patients for treatment at Port Hardy Hospital," said the jury, which added more emergency room training is needed for doctors and nurses in rural areas.
The jury suggested that ambulance attendants change their procedures, in future, so they consult with the matron or guard before transferring injured prisoners to hospital.

Public awareness programs should be developed and delivered to highlight social issues within Port Hardy, said a recommendation to community leaders in the District and the three First Nations communities around it.
Finally, the jury called for "the development of a sobering centre, detoxification centre" plus treatment safe houses and treatment facilities in Port Hardy."
